facts.text: Dog X presented for decreased drinking and general malaise; the triage abbreviation used was 'ADR.'
A fever was recorded; the ASR renders it as 'one of four seven,' which in context almost certainly represents 104.7°F, though the exact digits are garbled by the transcription.
Multiple ticks were found on Dog X during the examination; the staff described removing or treating them ('trying to roll that out').
A 4DX panel was sent and was still running at the time of the recorded discussion; results are not reported in any available block.
The dog was discharged with some medication, described in passing as something that 'works pretty quickly, even just a little medication.' The specific drug is not named in the available blocks.
The owner had the money but chose to use Care Credit for a payment plan; approximately seventy dollars could be deferred.
[recorded-reasoning] The treating clinician was Person, who was preparing the discharges while the owner's concern was being addressed.
The meaning of 'ADR' is never expanded in the available blocks. It is used as the triage reason but its full form is not stated.
